newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak cbank says no plans to boost reserves.
newsitem.headline: Slovak cbank says no plans to boost reserves.

text.p: The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) said on Wednesday it was not planning to take any international loans to boost its hard currency reserves saying current levels were adequate.
"We consider current reserves, enough for three months cover of imports, sufficient," NBS Governor Vladimir Masar told Reuters.
NBS foreign exchange reserves as of June 18 totalled $2.97 billion, up slightly from $2.93 billion as June 11.
Slovak imports totalled 123.178 billion crowns for the January-April period.

When asked whether the NBS was planning a similar move to the Czech central bank earlier this month when it took a $2.0 billion, one-year loan after its reserves were depleted by a crown crisis, Masar said: "Definitely no. We are not planning anything like this."
The Slovak crown has also been under pressure from speculators, but the NBS, through its daily fixing and a choking of market liquidity, has been able to ward off short-sellers.
Masar said that despite the high volatility on the interbank money market, the central bank's monetary policies appeared efficient enough to continue to battle any attacks on the crown.
He added the development of Slovak exports in his opinion was "fine" but said something needed to be done to suppress rising imports.
Slovakia's trade deficit stood at 27.9 billion crowns for the first five months of the year, up from 21.5 billion for the same period in 1996.
